items.title: 'Unprecedented' rain in Japan kills eight people
items.description: The storm cut power to more than 20,000 households and left 7,000 people stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport.

items.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
items.description: BBC's Top Comment podcast has found a network of Instagram profiles glamourising the swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence.

items.title: US says dozens of countries helped China dodge Trump's tariffs
items.description: A new US report said China had moved goods through nations with lower tariffs to dodge higher levies.

items.title: Builders unearth €9m gold stash sealed in walls of Belgian property
items.description: Construction workers found the stash in the walls of a cellar while drilling to lay sewage pipes.

items.title: Stolen Matisse artworks recovered by police in Brazil
items.description: A man is arrested after eight works by the French artist are found at a home in greater São Paulo.

items.title: Presidential vote counting halted in Zambia over alleged attacks on polling staff
items.description: The electoral commission said violence had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers".

items.title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
items.description: Thousands of sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

items.title: Engine parts smashed Ryanair window that man's head was sucked out of, report says
items.description: A preliminary report by US investigators says an engine fan blade broke on last month's flight from Greece to Germany.

items.title: US missionary released following kidnap in Niger, Christian group says
items.description: Kevin Rideout, who was kidnapped outside his home in the capital last October, is now with US officials.

items.title: Palestinians told to leave homes in village where Israeli settlers besieged houses
items.description: The mayor of Qusra says Israeli troops have been telling families to leave their houses, using some as barracks.

items.title: Person fined after using foghorn to wake sleeping polar bear
items.description: Under local regulations in the region, "it is forbidden to needlessly disturb, attract or pursue a polar bear".

items.title: Romania shuts only nuclear plant as heat causes huge drop in Danube River level
items.description: The Cernavodă plant, which produces 20% of Romania's electricity, is not expected to be restarted within the next 10 days.

items.title: Air India to test all pilots for banned substances
items.description: It comes after one of its planes suddenly lost altitude last week, with a number of passengers injured.

items.title: Four Canadian hockey stars remain suspended after sexual assault acquittal
items.description: A fifth has been reinstated, though an appeals board found that the whole group broke Hockey Canada's code of conduct.

items.title: Eurovision Song Contest 2027 to be held in Burgas, Bulgaria
items.description: The Black Sea location has been selected after Bulgarian singer Dara won this year's contest.

items.title: Teens who fled Venezuela after deadly quakes caught in another disaster in Colombia
items.description: Deivi Delfín and his brother moved to Colombia after a quake in Venezuela killed their mother, but were caught in another deadly disaster.

items.title: Indian solar mission's new findings throw light on enduring Sun mysteries
items.description: Why is the Sun's corona millions of degrees hotter than its surface? And how does it maintain its inexplicably high temperature?

items.title: Putin can no longer claim victory in Ukraine, Nobel Peace Prize winner tells BBC
items.description: In an exclusive interview with the BBC’s Steve Rosenberg, Dmitry Muratov says the Kremlin leader can only "destroy Ukraine, not conquer it", with the war now in its fifth year.

items.title: Who could replace White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt?
items.description: The job requires managing a complex relationship with the media - as well Trump's high expectations.

items.title: Vultures are disappearing in Nigeria - but the 'Vulture King' is fighting to reverse the trend
items.description: Some see them as sinister or hunt them for ritual use but these birds play a vital role in nature's cycle.
